data.title: Pi extension/shim: gwl-agents GitHub App identity for ephemeral agents
data.description:
DR 0011: ephemeral Pi agents use the gwl-agents GitHub App class identity. They need a way to run gh/git as gwl-agents[bot] without mutating Grey's stored gh auth.

Scope:
- A Pi extension if the extension API supports env/spawn hooks; otherwise a small shim directory prepended to PATH for agent subprocesses.
- Mint/refresh GitHub App installation access tokens (they expire ~1 hour) using the gwl-agents app credentials; never store a static GH_TOKEN in config.
- Inject GH_TOKEN per agent process, plus GH_CONFIG_DIR isolation if needed, and git author/committer env for gwl-agents[bot] once the renamed bot id/email is re-discovered.
- Respect the tightened permission set Grey configured (review-first + the two extras); document that Contents:write means agents can push on unprotected repos.
- Acceptance: an ephemeral Pi code-review subagent can post a PR review as gwl-agents[bot]; gh auth status as Grey remains unchanged outside the agent process.

Context: hearth DR 0011 (GitHub identity) and tmp/github-identity-spike-2026-08-15.md.

data.title: Multiple gwl-agents GitHub Apps: per-agent identities so parallel reviews don't collapse
data.description:
Problem: parallel review agents (the multi-review skill) all post to GitHub as the single `gwl-agents` app. GitHub computes `reviewDecision` from the latest review per reviewer *identity*, so all agents collapse into one reviewer and the last review wins — a later APPROVE from one agent silently overrides an earlier CHANGES_REQUESTED from another, hiding blocking findings in the aggregate badge.

Observed 2026-09-09 on gwl-job-tools PRs #19/#21/#22: deepseek-v4-pro posted CHANGES_REQUESTED, glm-5.3-flash posted APPROVED seconds later, and the PR's reviewDecision flipped to APPROVED even though the blocking review is still in the review list.

Improvement:
- Provision one GitHub App per agent identity (e.g. gwl-agents-arch / -logic / -sec, or per-model), each installed on the same repos with the same tightened permission set.
- Extend the gh-app wrapper (or the GWLA-fi1m8w shim) to select the app identity per agent (env var / flag / per-agent config), so each parallel reviewer posts under a distinct identity.
- Update the gh-app skill: document identity selection and the "one identity per agent" rule.
- Update the multi-review skill: external-PR workflow should have each reviewer post its own review under its own identity (or explicitly document that the build agent posts a single consolidated review), and note the reviewDecision last-wins caveat.
- Update global agent instructions (AGENTS.md) if they reference the single-app rule.

Acceptance: two parallel agents posting different verdicts on the same PR produce a reviewDecision that reflects the blocking verdict (a CHANGES_REQUESTED is not overridden by a later APPROVE from a different identity).

Related: GWLA-fi1m8w (single-app shim — the foundation this builds on).

data.description: Unknown: what pb claim does mechanically when an issue is already in_progress — does it fail, steal, or no-op? Does it distinguish 'claimed by me earlier' from 'claimed by another agent'? Relevant for multi-agent worktree workflows. The pebble-skill updates this was tabled behind have landed (PRs #3–#5, bucket-epic convention), so it is ripe to explore together against the CLI source at /home/grey/Source/external/pebble/ and document in the skill.

data.text: Updated: pebble CLI source moved to /home/grey/Source/external/pebble/. Also noting the tabled-behind condition is satisfied — the pebble-skill updates have all merged.

Explored against CLI source (v0.2.0, state.ts claimWithCascade + types.ts), verified empirically in a sandbox. Findings: (1) Re-claim is a NO-OP SUCCESS, not a steal — claim skips any target already in_progress and returns success with claimedIds:[] (or containing only newly-cascaded parents). pb claim is not a lock and provides no contention protection. (2) No claimer/assignee concept in the data model; in_progress is the only work-in-flight signal; comment 'author' field exists but the CLI never sets it. Event 'source' records the worktree/folder name, not an agent identity — so 'mine vs another agent' is indistinguishable from the ledger. (3) Useful nuance: empty claimedIds distinguishes a no-op from a fresh claim; re-claiming a child whose parent reverted to open re-claims the parent (cascade is a repair mechanism). (4) Guards verified: cannot claim closed/deleted/blocked-target/blocked-ancestor issues; blocked is determined by open blockedBy deps, not status — an issue with status 'blocked' but no blockers IS claimable; pb update --status in_progress has the same guard (no bypass). Skill documentation to follow in the pending rewrite; keeping this issue in_progress until that lands.

Rewritten claim section documents the findings: claiming-flags-not-locking semantics, claimedIds response reading, source-based attribution check, surface-and-proceed contention protocol, cascade-repair nuance, and the blocked-by-dependency-not-status rule. Landed in commit ac27e37 on branch pebble-rewrite (PR pending); will close once merged.

Promotion criteria (from the record's ## Promotion): (1) at least two records besides DR-0001 exist, each recording a decision made in non-bootstrap work and each cited by id in the commit subject of the change that acted on it; (2) drs.py check --strict has passed on main at every commit touching docs/decisions, per CI history. data.text: First contact with real use found a deadlock before any record existed: drs.py index writes unpadded tables, dprint pads them, so the two fail each other's checks in a loop (index -> dprint check fails; dprint fmt -> drs check says stale). Fixed by emitting <!-- dprint-ignore-file --> as the index's first line: generator owns the generated view, records stay formatted. PR #11 (5ed9c03), 79 tests, CI green.

First real-use finding, corrected: the index/formatter deadlock was OUR contract, not the formatter. Byte-identical index comparison cannot coexist with a readable (formatter-aligned) index. #11 (dprint-ignore-file) closed as the wrong trade; #12 replaces byte comparison with content comparison - every record has a row, no foreign rows, and each row's link/title/decision/state match; padding, alignment, row order and preamble are not staleness. 84 tests, CI green.

Closing the promotion task I filed for DR-0001. The record was written as a test of the decisions protocol against a fresh corpus (it surfaced the index/formatter deadlock); Grey confirmed it was never intended to land, because this repo does not ship records for review. DR-0001 stays on branch adopt-decision-records as a reading artifact. Reopen if adoption is ever revisited.

data.title: drs: property test that generated output always passes its own audit
data.description:
Three review rounds in a row found the same defect class: drs.py index (or drs.py new) can emit something drs.py check rejects, and regeneration cannot fix it. Round 3: new-vs-parser round trip. Round 4: sections, duplicate rows, missing marker. Round 5: pipes in legacy filenames, surrounding whitespace in title/summary. Each fix was small; the class keeps recurring because the generator and the audit are separate code paths and nothing exercises the round trip through the CLI.

Proposal: a property test over a corpus of hostile-but-valid records (legacy filenames with pipes/parens/spaces/unicode, padded and quoted fields, all five states, amendments and supersessions, escaped pipes in titles) that, for each fixture: run index, then check, and assert zero errors; then run dprint fmt equivalent (or simulate padding) and assert check still zero errors; then assert the record set round-trips through parse_index. Cheap to write, would have caught rounds 3, 4 and 5 in one go.

data.text: SHIPPED PR #12 (04570c3, local fast-forward): index checked by content with sections, duplicate detection, required marker, escaped pipes, whitespace rejection, truthful line numbers. 98 tests. Both CHANGES_REQUESTED reviews dismissed (addressed in ca867c0 / 23231f2, Grey approved out-of-band). CI green on main post-merge (run 45433349238). Worktree, branch and stale remote branch removed.
Filed from review round 5: three consecutive rounds found generator-output-rejected-by-its-own-audit defects. This is the harness idea that would have caught all three.

Found by auditing gwl-systems for adoption: SKILL.md's adoption section warned that renaming breaks inbound links, but the tooling section said 'relative links resolve' as if that were general. The check is one-directional (record body -> target only), so a rename leaves specs/Ansible/code comments dead while the audit stays green -- 74 inbound refs in gwl-systems. Docs fix in PR #13.

PR #13 merged (b0e0d09, local fast-forward, CI green run 45435297253): SKILL.md now says the link check is one-directional and that a rename is repository-wide. Worktree/branch/remote branch cleaned up. Only main remains.

data.title: decisions: first full retrofit exposes formatter and adoption protocol bugs
data.description:
Found during the first full real-repository adoption, in gwl-systems PR #57 (https://github.com/plathrop/gwl-systems/pull/57): 17 legacy records retrofitted in place, two new records added, and the generated index checked with drs.py. The core lifecycle/graph checks worked, but adoption exposed protocol gaps that the current guide and tool do not cover safely.

## 1. Formatter suppression is not an answer — protocol bug

A realistic full-adoption record has a long legacy_bodies flow sequence. dprint's YAML formatter wraps it across lines; drs.py deliberately accepts only a one-line flow sequence. The formatted record then fails to parse, all legacy exemptions disappear, and one formatting pass cascades into 70 errors.

Using dprint-ignore-file (or any formatter-ignore/suppression directive) on the adoption record is NOT an acceptable resolution. It exempts the most important new record from the repository's formatting contract and repeats the already-rejected generated-index trade in a new place. The skill currently gives no warning against this move; that omission is itself a bug in the protocol.

Required:
- SKILL.md must explicitly say that disabling, ignoring, or suppressing the repository formatter is not a valid way to make a decision record pass drs.py.
- Change the format/tool contract so an ordinarily formatted full-adoption record remains valid, without suppressing formatting and without falsifying or omitting legacy_bodies entries.
- Add a regression test that formats a realistic adoption record with enough legacy_bodies ids to exceed the line width, then runs drs.py check and requires zero errors. Relate this to GWLA-ltukr0's generator/audit round-trip coverage.
- Until the upstream fix lands, gwl-systems DR-0019 carries a temporary dprint-ignore-file marker after its front matter. Remove that workaround in the adopting repo once a real protocol/tool fix exists; do not bless it as the pattern.

## 2. `new` silently ignores an unmanaged legacy corpus

On the initial all-legacy corpus, drs.py new saw zero managed records and scaffolded DR-0001. That is the correct next number only after existing files receive their ids; running it first creates renumbering work and could collide with the intended chronological allocation. Nothing in the command output or adoption steps warns about this ordering dependency.

Choose and document a guard: preferably new warns or refuses when unmanaged Markdown records are present, or the adoption protocol makes "add front matter before using new" an explicit ordered requirement. Add a CLI-level regression test for the chosen behavior.

Positive control: after the legacy front matter was installed, new consistently allocated the next ids, and a scratch post-adoption probe allocated DR-0020 as Draft with no invented reviewer.

## 3. Historical supersession by a change has no record-level target

DR-0003 (Python environment) already said Superseded by the archived self-contained-ansible-runtime change, but no successor decision record existed. The new schema requires status.by to name a record and checks the supersession edge in both directions. Pointing status.by at the adoption record would falsely claim adoption caused the historical reversal; leaving the old record Accepted would falsify its standing.

The adoption guide needs an explicit procedure for this shape. In PR #57, DR-0018 reconstructs the real successor decision from the archived proposal/design and PR #14 review, retaining the original decision date and carrying the old position in Alternatives. This is distinct from copying an unchanged legacy decision forward under a false supersession. The guide should explain that distinction, what evidence is required, and how this interacts with the writing guidance not to manufacture records for already-implemented decisions.

## 4. Tool availability and reproducibility need an explicit adoption choice

The canonical tool is supplied by the installed skill rather than the adopting repository. That avoids a fork, but the installed skill version becomes part of the authoring environment and command examples otherwise depend on a machine-specific skill path. Document the expected invocation/discovery model and whether adopters should reference the installed skill, pin a copy, or use another supported entry point. Do not silently normalize an unversioned repo-local fork.

## What worked and should remain covered

- The content-based index comparison accepted dprint-aligned tables while still detecting content drift.
- Supersession edges, legacy exemptions, canonical-heading checks, and relative outbound-link checks were consistent.
- check --strict correctly left permanent legacy warnings as warnings while returning zero errors.
- All 98 bundled drs.py tests passed before this follow-up.

Acceptance for this pebble is not merely documenting the observed friction: items 1-3 need explicit protocol decisions, matching tool/guide changes where applicable, and regression tests. Item 1 must state the no-formatter-suppression rule in SKILL.md itself.

data.text: Priority raised P2 -> P1 on Grey's call: this blocked completing the adoption PR cleanly, and we worked around it with a formatter-ignore marker we now have to remove. Fixes in PR #14: parser accepts formatter output (wrapped flow + trailing comma + block), no-suppression rule in SKILL.md, 'new' warns on unmanaged corpora, reconstruction procedure, tool identity via --version. CI round-trip harness added (roundtrip.sh in the format job) as the narrow half of GWLA-ltukr0.

Narrow half landed in PR #14: decisions/tests/roundtrip.sh runs dprint over a generated 17-record corpus in the CI format job and requires drs.py check to pass, verifying the list actually wrapped so the test cannot stop proving anything. The hostile-corpus property test (pipes, parens, unicode, all states, amendments) is still this pebble's remaining scope.

Additional hostile-parser cases found while reviewing PR #14 (head 4952f27), deliberately not added to that PR's already-satisfied adoption scope:

1. `legacy_bodies: ["DR-0001",,]` parses as `['DR-0001']`: parse_scalar removes all trailing empty items rather than exactly the one produced by a legal trailing comma. Invalid repeated commas should be rejected.
2. A comment between items in a wrapped flow list is collected as data: `['legacy_bodies: [', '  "DR-0001",', '  # comment', '  "DR-0002",', ']']` produces a second value containing `# comment\n  "DR-0002"` instead of either ignoring the comment or rejecting the shape clearly.
3. A blank line between block-sequence items ends collection; the next indented item is then reported as an unrelated indentation error. Either support legal blank/comment separators or explicitly reject/document them.

These do not affect the verified dprint seventeen-id round trip, but they are concrete fixtures for this task's hostile-corpus property test. The desired behavior can be strict rejection rather than broader YAML support; it should be deliberate and tested, not accidental misparsing.

Reviewed and APPROVED gwl-agent-skills PR #14 at 4952f27 as kimi-k3.1-pro. It addresses all four findings: formatter-compatible sequences plus an explicit no-suppression rule in SKILL.md; unmanaged-corpus warning and ordered adoption; an evidence-based reconstruction procedure; canonical installed-tool guidance and --version identity.

Local evidence: 106 tests, real dprint round trip, dprint check, and diff check all pass; all three GitHub checks green. Decisive real-corpus probe: copied gwl-systems PR #57's records to scratch, removed DR-0019's ignore directive, formatted with gwl-systems' dprint config, and the new tool reported 19 records / 0 errors under --strict with 68 expected legacy warnings. The formatted corpus passes dprint.

data.title: drs: adopt command for the mechanical half of a retrofit
data.description: From the second adoption run (GWLA-cyo1hs follow-up, gwl-systems #58): a full retrofit is 17 bespoke front-matter edits, done with a throwaway script. Proposed: 'drs.py adopt <file> --id --date --summary' that prepends a validated front-matter block, refuses if the body would change (byte-comparison of the body before and after), refuses if the file already has front matter, and requires --summary because that is the judgement field. Report as a dry-run table by default and --write to apply. Design questions to settle: how it proves body preservation, how it handles a file whose first heading is not canonical, and whether it should refuse when the id it would assign is already taken. Pairs with the retrofit ordering requirement in the adoption section.

data.title: decisions: 'Draft' conflates unratified with unproven — decide the two promotion shapes
data.description:
SKILL.md defines Draft twice, in two incompatible ways, and a third adoption (flint, DR-0007) has now had to invent the reconciliation locally.

THE CONTRADICTION IS IN THE TOOL'S OWN WORDS:
- Lifecycle table: 'Decided in principle; reality has not tested it yet', with ## Promotion required on every Draft and 'Wait and see' explicitly rejected as a criterion. That is a PROBATION reading: the record is ratified (it has reviewers) but reality has not tested it.
- Front-matter table, reviewers row: 'Empty only while the record is a Draft — a record nobody ratified is a draft.' That is a REVIEW reading: the record exists, nobody has ratified it yet.

The same state carries both, so every Draft must satisfy both readings at once: a record awaiting review has to name observable-behavioral promotion criteria it cannot have. Each adopter has resolved it differently:
- gwl-agent-skills GWLA-cw7ew7 (DR-0001 promotion) used the probation reading — criteria were 'two more records exist and check --strict passed on main' — and its closing note records that this repo does not ship records for review.
- gwl-systems DR-0019's 'Land it Draft' alternative has the losing argument written down: the promotion gate and the merge were the same event.
- flint DR-0007 adopted a two-kinds reading (## Promotion names which kind it is: ratification-by-review, or a behavioral bet with tracked promotion work) because that was the only shape that kept the reviewers field honest without making every record carry a pro-forma Promotion paragraph.

WHAT NEEDS DECIDING (this is a protocol decision, so it wants a DR in this repo, not just a text edit):
1. Is Draft one state with two documented flavors, or two states? If two, name them and say what drs.py requires for each — note that 'Promotion required on Draft' is what forces the pro-forma paragraph for review-pending records.
2. Whichever way it goes, what does 'reviewers' mean when it is empty, and may a review-pending record be committed at all? (flint's answer: no — a record awaiting ratification is never merged in that state, merging is the promotion.)
3. Interaction with the rule that a promoted draft KEEPS its ## Promotion section: if the common case is review-pending, every accepted record in an adopting repo ends up carrying a one-line Promotion paragraph forever. Is that intended, or should the section be optional once state is Accepted?
4. Test coverage: drs.py should be able to tell a well-formed ratification criterion from a well-formed behavioral one, or it should stop implying it can.

EVIDENCE TO USE: flint DR-0007 (the two-kinds shape, written and checked), gwl-systems DR-0019 Alternatives, GWLA-cw7ew7's closing comment. Note also that the skill's own text already asserts the review reading, so this is not a new interpretation — it is two existing interpretations that were never reconciled.

data.title: decisions: no adopter can run the audit in CI while the tool is 'never vendored'
data.description:
GWLA-cyo1hs item 4 was closed by PR #14 as 'canonical installed-tool guidance and --version identity'. That answers AUTHORING. It does not answer CI, and flint's adoption (DR-0007, 2026-11-26) is the second adopter to hit the wall.

THE PROBLEM: SKILL.md forbids vendoring drs.py ('a repo-local fork is a second implementation that has to be maintained deliberately, and an unversioned one is worse than no tool') and names the installed skill path as canonical. But a CI runner has no installed skill. So every adopter that wants the audit enforced picks from three bad options: (a) install the skill in the runner — nothing installable exists; (b) vendor a copy — forbidden by the skill; (c) reimplement the checks — a second implementation, which is the thing vendoring was rejected for. Meanwhile the protocol claims a stale index is an error, and nothing in any adopting repo can fail on it.

WHAT IS AND IS NOT SOLVED TODAY:
- Identity is fine: drs.py --version prints a content hash (7d0bb223e7f3 = sha256 of the script), so 'which tool' is answerable.
- Distribution is not: 'git tag' lists zero tags in this repo, there is no package, and the usual install is a symlink into a working checkout (~/.pi/agent/decisions -> ~/Source/gwl-agent-skills/decisions/). So 'pinned to 7d0bb223e7f3' names a file's contents, not a fetchable artifact; a CI cannot retrieve that revision without cloning and knowing the commit.
- Scope is also not solved: the hash covers drs.py only. SKILL.md can change, including rules the audit assumes, with the same tool hash — so an adopter's record citing the hash does not pin the protocol it was written against.

EVIDENCE OF SYSTEMIC-NESS: gwl-systems GWLS-o4zbi3 (audit not yet run anywhere) and flint FLIN-5xe4yp (filed 2026-11-26, deferred by DR-0007 as 'deliberately not done here') are both adopters waiting on this decision. This repo's own CI is not evidence: it runs drs from a checkout, where the tool is in-tree.

WHAT NEEDS DECIDING (protocol decision, wants a DR here):
1. Distribution: tag releases (so an adopter pins a ref), publish an installable artifact, or bless a vendor-with-pinned-hash mode and say what 'pinned' means. The skill currently rejects all three implicitly by rejecting the third explicitly.
2. Whether skill identity should cover the protocol or only the tool, and how an adopter records it.
3. The CI recipe adopters should copy — including whether the audit is expected to run at all in an adopting repo, or whether 'the habit' is the sanctioned end state. If the latter, SKILL.md's 'a stale index is an error' needs to say 'an error you cannot automate', because right now it reads as a promise.

Do not resolve this by loosening the no-vendoring rule without a decision: the reason for it (one implementation, maintained deliberately) is sound, and the gap is a missing release process, not a wrong rule.

data.text: Post-hoc note on this close: the reading artifact DR-0001 is unrecoverable. It was left on branch adopt-decision-records and never tagged; that branch is now gone locally and from origin, docs/decisions never appears anywhere in main's history, and git fsck finds no dangling commit holding it. A tag before deletion would have cost nothing and would have made 'the record stays on a branch' a durable statement instead of a stale pointer. Recording it so a future session does not go looking — if adoption is ever revisited, DR-0001 gets rewritten, not recovered.

data.text: Reframed 2026-11-26: this no longer asks for a decision record. We considered adopting records in this repo and declined — the rationale is in the resolution entry landing in decisions/README.md, and in short: SKILL.md is the artifact adopters actually load, so a records directory here would be invisible to the reader it is meant for, and this repo has no review tradition for a record's reviewers field to mean anything. The decision still needs stating; it must not be resolved by quiet text edit with the rejected option dropped.

Reframed 2026-11-26: resolution lands in SKILL.md plus a dated evidence entry, not a decision record — same call as on GWLA-4ybix9. Note this pebble's own subject is why the call went that way: adopting records here would have had to pick one reading of Draft before this pebble decided which reading is right.

Parking a versioning analysis discussed 2026-11-26 (decided: not what we are doing today; this comment is the record so it is not re-derived).

THE HAZARD, named concretely: adopters symlink a working checkout (~/.pi/agent/skills/decisions -> ~/Source/gwl-agent-skills/decisions/), so a `git pull` in the source checkout silently replaces the protocol under every adopter mid-work, with no signal. The two changes landed in PR #16/draft-semantics on 2026-11-26 would have arrived that way.

THREE THINGS THAT MAKE IT MILDER THAN IT SOUNDS:
1. The failure mode is loud. The format is checkable, so an incompatible change turns an adopter's CI red on the next run instead of silently corrupting records.
2. `drs.py --version` already content-hashes the tool, so "which tool" is answerable.
3. A version number with one consumer is speculation: semver needs a decision about what counts as major FOR ADOPTERS YOU DO NOT HAVE. The only thing we could say is "something changed", which a hash says better and without anyone remembering to bump it.

RECOMMENDATION (answers this pebble's question 2, "should identity cover the protocol or only the tool"): not semver, not tags.
- Extend `--version` to hash the whole skill directory, not just the script, so protocol identity covers SKILL.md and assets. Today `drs.py 7d0bb223e7f3` lets SKILL.md change under a pinned hash, which is this pebble's scope complaint; the fix is ~5 lines. Citation then reads like an adoption record pinning the rules it was written against.
- Add a compatibility corpus: records in every shape the protocol has ever accepted (Draft carrying a ## Promotion section, wrapped flow lists, dated legacy filenames, all five states, single-and-multi reviewers), all required to keep passing `check` with zero errors. A change that turns it red is by construction a breaking change, so the author decides knowingly rather than discovering it in an adopter's CI. Same harness family as GWLA-ltukr0, aimed at compatibility rather than generator/auditor round-tripping.
- Skip git tags FOR THIS PURPOSE. Tags buy distribution and CI pinning, which is a real need but the other half of this pebble; do not solve two problems with one ceremony.

The promise alternative: semver's real value is not the number but the commitment "your corpus keeps working until the major bumps". One line in SKILL.md states it without a version and the compatibility corpus makes it testable: the tool never silently invalidates a corpus that passed the audit before.

TRIGGER TO REVISIT: when a second real adopter exists and can be broken by something. Then mint versions from the compatibility corpus's revisions, because "major" finally means someone is on the wrong side of it.

EVIDENCE THAT TODAY'S CHANGES WERE SAFE: ran old and new drs.py against every corpus on this machine on 2026-11-26 — gwl-systems 22 records / 0 errors / 68 warnings, flint 7 / 0 / 1, dotfiles 0 / 1 / 1. Identical under both tools, because the changes only removed requirements and the one added requirement (reviewers non-empty) was already satisfied by all 29 records.
